mission_01: TPUs (Tensor Processing Units) are Google's custom AI accelerators built around a systolic array architecture for efficient matrix multiplication. Unlike CPUs that fetch and execute instructions sequentially, a TPU's systolic array is a grid of processing elements (PEs) where data flows rhythmically through the array. Each PE performs a multiply-accumulate operation: C[i,j] += A[i,k] * B[k,j]. The key insight is that at each timestep k, a column of A and a row of B are broadcast across the array, and all PEs simultaneously compute their partial products. This achieves O(1) arithmetic intensity per PE and maximizes hardware utilization. In this mission, you simulate a systolic array by iterating over the contraction dimension, computing outer products at each timestep, and accumulating results. You also implement bfloat16 quantization simulation, throughput estimation, and comparison with standard CPU matrix multiplication.
